textbookText: Since the refractive index of glass with respect to air is greater than that with respect to water, the power of lens decreases when it is immerged in water.
Q. An air bubble is formed inside water. If refraction of light takes place through this
bubble, does it act as a converging lens or a diverging lens?
According to the lens maker formula, the focal length of the lens is given by,
= ( – 1)  +  . Where,  is the refractive index of air lens with respect to the water.
Here < 1 and hence f becomes negative. This means light rays will diverge in such
arrangement. Therefore, air bubble inside water will act as a diverging lens.
But due to total internal reflection air bubbles commonly glow inside water.

17.6 Power of a Lens Do you know why some people in your locality use spectacles? Do you know the power of the lens they used in their spectacles?

Every ray of light falling on the convex lens deviates towards the principal axis and tends to converge, but every ray of light falling on the concave lens deviates away from the principal axis and tends to diverge. Therefore, the main function of the lens is to deviate the light rays incident on it and hence power of a lens is measured in terms of its ability to deviate the rays.

The ability of a lens to converge or diverge a ray of light after refraction through it is called the power of that lens. It is defined as the reciprocal of focal length. A lens of a short focal length produces more deviation than that of a lens of a larger focal length as shown in figure 17.7. Lens L2 has less focal length than lens L1 so that L2 bends the rays more than L1, and the power of lens L2 is greater than that of L1. 1 power (p) = f [Fig.17.7, Ray diagram for measurement the power of lens]
